tells.1: Vague, reassuring filler such as 'guidance you can trust', 'keep your recovery moving' and 'unlock more of what the app has to offer', plus a benefit-explaining 'so...' clause on every bullet.
tells.2: Casual phrasing that feels forced ('Maybe you're bouncing back', 'we'll give you a nudge', 'keep you moving forward') layered over the same templated 'so...' bullet structure.
tells.4: Over-flattened, mechanical declaratives ('Each video shows the form for the movement') and stacked 'so...' clauses that read like de-fluffed AI copy with the voice removed.
tells.5: Mild stock phrasing ('know what to do and how to do it right', 'see how far you've come').

reason: Version 3 has the quirks of real App Store copy: hyphenated label bullets, an exclamation mark, 'Never miss a session again' and Apple's boilerplate renewal wording. But that boilerplate is clunky and the hype weakens credibility. Version 5 keeps the clean structure and accurate subscription terms while cutting the vague promises and filler of versions 1 and 2, so it's the strongest one to publish.
